card.title: Addition vs substitution — the π-bond decides

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Alkanes substitute by free radicals (halogenation) and burn; alkenes/alkynes ADD across π bonds following Markovnikov (stable-carbocation path) with HBr-peroxide reversal; terminal alkynes donate ≡C–H (acidic, Ag/Cu salts). Benzene refuses addition (aromaticity worth ~150 kJ/mol) and substitutes electrophilically instead — nitration, sulphonation, halogenation, Friedel–Crafts — with directors choosing ortho/para or meta.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Markovnikov: H→H-rich C (carbocation stability 3°>2°>1°) · peroxide: HBr only, reversed  ·  ozonolysis: C=C → 2 C=O (skeleton proof)  ·  benzene: E⁺ replaces H, ring intact · activators o/p (OH, NH₂, alkyl) · deactivators meta (NO₂, COOH) · conformations: staggered > gauche > eclipsed

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Markovnikov needs unsymmetrical alkene + ionic HX; peroxide reversal is HBr-only. Ozonolysis needs reductive workup (Zn/H₂O) for aldehydes/ketones. Benzene substitution needs generated electrophiles (NO₂⁺, Br⁺/FeBr₃, R⁺/AlCl₃) — plain Br₂ water does nothing (the alkene distinction test). Conformation analysis rotates around σ bonds only.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Ozonolysis fragments map the old double bond (but-2-ene → 2 ethanal). Acetylene's acidity gives white Ag₂C₂ / red Cu₂C₂ precipitates. Phenol brominates without catalyst (super-activated); benzene needs FeBr₃. Polymerisation (Ziegler–Natta) chains ethene into polythene.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Propene + HBr: protonate to the 2° carbocation (CH₃–C⁺H–CH₃, not primary) → Br⁻ captures → 2-bromopropane (Markovnikov). With peroxides: Br· adds first to give the more stable carbon radical → 1-bromopropane (anti-Markovnikov). Same substrate, opposite products — mechanism written, marks banked.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Carbocation rearrangements (hydride/methyl shifts) rewrite Markovnikov predictions. Free-radical halogenation gives mixtures (selectivity only biases). Wurtz couples symmetrically or statistically. Benzene's orientation rules guide; o/p splits still need separation.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Electrophilic addition via the lower-energy carbocation (hyperconjugation + +I count decides) — product ratios follow intermediate stability, hence the rule. Benzene's arenium ion delocalises over three carbons (draw all forms); restoring aromaticity by deprotonation beats addition by the resonance energy — substitution derived, not decreed.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Symmetrical substrate? Rule moot, one product. Ozonolysis: join carbonyl carbons back with C=C. Benzene + Br₂ water → no reaction (vs alkenes bleach) — the distinction MCQ. Conformations: staggered minimum, eclipsed maximum, always.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: Markovnikov vs peroxide-effect pairs; ozonolysis structure proof; benzene nitration/sulphonation/Friedel–Crafts with orientation; alkyne acidity tests; conformations energy order.
